reviews.text: This game is why I love Steam's little recommendation carousel. Occasionally you get a real gem like this. It's a Korean Mythology roguelike with multiple characters and storylines. It couldn't be more laser focused to me if it tried. It's FREE. Give it a shot, enjoy a fun run through another cultures history and myths, and slay some naughty demons.

Mangui is the kind of game that doesn’t try to be too much—it’s short, sweet, and sticks to its strengths. At its core, it’s a lighthearted experience that’s easy to pick up and play, offering just enough charm to keep you entertained without demanding too much from you. The gameplay is straightforward, leaning into casual mechanics that make it accessible to just about anyone. It’s not particularly deep, and you might find yourself wishing for a bit more variety after a while, but what’s there is polished and enjoyable. It’s the kind of game you’d play to unwind, not to test your skills or dive into a long session. Visually, Mangui has a cute and colorful style that feels inviting. The animations are smooth, and there’s a certain warmth in the way everything is presented. The music is pleasant, though it leans a bit repetitive, especially if you’re playing for an extended period. The biggest strength of Mangui is its laid-back vibe. It knows what it is and doesn’t overcomplicate things, which is refreshing in a world of games that sometimes try to do too much. That said, if you’re looking for something more challenging or complex, you might find it lacking. Overall, Mangui is a nice little escape—a game that’s fun for what it is, even if it doesn’t leave a lasting impression. If you’re in the mood for something light and cheerful, it’s worth giving a try.

Better than most 10 dollar I see. The story though generic but the art style more than make up for it to become a epic adventure. The game never over states it's welcome with the length of it's run. The game combat is surprisingly deep and challenging. I almost die once every chapter to heat the game on the easiest difficulty. It almost resemble dark soul with it requiring player to learn it's enemy's attack and movement pattern to survival. The enemy variety is also plenty for what is supposed to be a very early access free game. With some light on this gem, I believe this game can do well even even as a full $8 1.0 release.

Pro: -Pretty fun rogue-like game. -Unique Korean mythology stories. -The art style is great and distinctive. -I love simple pixel-art styles! Feedbacks: -Would be nice to be able to rebind the skill keys, as the 1~5 number keys are a bit awkward to press. -Sometimes it's a bit hard to discern which are wall tiles and which are the ground. Maybe highlight the walls when the character is adjacent. -The vision fog is nice but might be a bit difficult to navigate. I suggest keeping the explored map dimmed but visible instead of being completely obscured by the fog. -The skill tree could be presented more clearly to show which skills are linked and needed to unlock the next tier, Will update this review as I finish the story.

虽然优化还有点小问题，比如对话中的贴图有时候会遮蔽文本，又或者不能设定按键这种小问题，但估计开发是小团队，所以完全可以理解。 玩法上感觉有之前玩过的某个flash小游戏的影子，但是自己做了进一步的改造延申，加了不同的职业和技能，可玩性要好得多。 最让我印象深刻的是文本，看得出来开发或者编剧涉猎挺广的，涉及到韩国乃至中国或者说东亚的各种历史和传说，四个人物都有自己的性格特点，以及完全不同的思维模式和人生轨迹。其中又有一些想法，比如孝道、忠君之类的，大部分对历史文化感兴趣的东亚人都会会心一笑吧。 很不错的小游戏，期待作者其他的作品。

这款转型买断制的回合制肉鸽游戏，用中式恐怖+山海经美学劈开一条新赛道。我们扮演的驱魔人以符咒、铜钱剑与五行术对抗魑魅魍魉，战斗系统堪称《杀戮尖塔》遇上《林正英宇宙》，蜈蚣女王需火符破甲后贴镇尸符，影子将军则要用八卦镜反弹其影刃，每场BOSS战都是民俗学考试现场。 叙事野心比它的纸人更立体：通过轮回机制拼凑山村灭门惨案真相，支线任务里与吊死鬼讨价还价、给狐仙当红娘的黑色幽默，让阴森氛围里透出《聊斋》式的人性微光。对比《Hades》的希腊神话狂欢，《Mangui》的「三魂七魄」成长树更讲究阴阳平衡，过度使用禁术会招致厉鬼反噬，逼玩家在道法自然与速通诱惑间反复横跳。 缺陷如同它的僵尸般僵硬，后期重复的赶尸小游戏、未中文化的古籍残卷谜题，让非东方文化圈玩家宛如面对天书符咒。但24小时峰值在线数证明，当结尾动画里主角焚烧契约遁入轮回时，我们买的不仅是游戏，更是一场对《子不语》时代的蒸汽朋克朝圣。

It seems they gave it away for free and I either didn’t know or forgot to claim it. I don’t regret missing out, as I rarely pay attention to freebies, and I’m glad I bought it in the end. The game is a linear roguelike that consists of three story chapters and can be played by any of four characters. The only drawback IMO, is that there is no save function, so you have to finish a chapter in one go, which can take up to an hour. Apart from that, I find everything else positive. The story, based on Korean folklore, sounds a bit strange but has an undeniable personality, along the distinctive style of the characters art. For me, the standout elements are the soundtrack, which is excellent, and the gameplay, which feels really good. The turn‑based combat is very easy to get the hang of, so you can play at your own pace and adjust your focus according to enemy difficulty. The item and skill systems are also intuitive, making the game enjoyable from the first minute. I highly recommend giving it a go. You can download a demo if you are unsure, and if you happen to get the full game for free, be sure to give it the chance it deserves. For those who look back at a game like Cardinal Quest 2 and want something similar, Mangui might be something to fill that void. The gameplay mechanics are similar enough that you can see the direct inspiration, yet at the same time it also adds its own twist on things. Featuring a theme rooted in Korean mythology, the game doesn't really have any sort of dungeon diving going on, as you romp around on an outdoor environment. The enemies feature a fairly interesting set of pros and cons, leading the player to have to manage how they approach combat. The above said, while it does have a lot to like, there is a lot to consider before picking up this title.... First, this is a game without procedural generation. This means that you will trudging in the same maps over and over again. There also doesn't seem to be any randomization of enemies either, so you'll likely also be facing the exact same number of enemies on each map. A big part of roguelikes is that you can play them again and again - this title is moreso one that you might play once. And unfortunately that leads into another issue with this game... The second issue being the unlock system. At the start of the game you can only play with two of the four classes. You also only have access to the first story for each of them and can only play the game on the easiest and intended difficulties. If you want to play with Domak or Damulchi, be prepared to play through the entire story first with Yoon Gil or Jang Gosari to unlock them. Want to play a harder difficulty? The requires beating the game with the preceding difficulty first. You also need to beat a story on normal difficulty if you want to play subsequent stories on normal too... It is for these issues that this review is being marked as a recommendation against picking this title up. I might also consider the price a little high too, considering how cheap Cardinal Quest 2 is now, but that seems fairly minor.
